description: CAG, UPSC, Election Commission — appointment, tenure, functions

questions.stem: The COMPTROLLER AND AUDITOR GENERAL of India is appointed under Article:
questions.explanation: Article 148 — CAG. Article 280 — Finance Commission. Article 324 — Election Commission. Article 315 — UPSC. CAG has a 6-year term or up to age 65 (whichever earlier), appointed by the President and removable only like a SC judge.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Constitutional bodies (CAG, UPSC, EC) — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called WHICH OFFICE 'the most important officer under the Constitution of India'?
questions.explanation: Ambedkar called the CAG the 'most important officer'. Reason: accountability of the executive to the legislature hinges on independent audit. CAG submits reports to the President/Governor, which are placed before Parliament/Legislature and then examined by the PAC.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Constitutional bodies (CAG, UPSC, EC) — mixed tiers

questions.stem: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) was first set up as the PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION in the year:
questions.explanation: Public Service Commission established 1 October 1926 on Lee Commission recommendation (1923-24). Renamed 'Federal PSC' under GoI Act 1935. Renamed 'UPSC' at the start of the Constitution (26 January 1950). Constituted under Article 315.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Constitutional bodies (CAG, UPSC, EC) — mixed tiers

questions.stem: The ELECTION COMMISSION of India is:
questions.explanation: ECI is set up under Article 324 (hence constitutional, not statutory). Conducts elections to Parliament, state legislatures, and President/VP. Became multi-member (CEC + 2 ECs) from 1993 onwards. All three commissioners have equal voting power.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Constitutional bodies (CAG, UPSC, EC) — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Match the CONSTITUTIONAL BODY with its ARTICLE. A. Attorney General.  B. Finance Commission.  C. Election Commission.  D. CAG. List-II: 1. Article 76.  2. Article 280.  3. Article 324.  4. Article 148.
questions.explanation: AG — Art 76. FC — Art 280. EC — Art 324. CAG — Art 148. (Advocate General of State — Art 165; UPSC — Art 315; Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities — Art 350B.)
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Constitutional bodies (CAG, UPSC, EC) — mixed tiers

questions.stem: The TENURE of a Chief Election Commissioner of India is:

options.option_text: 5 years or up to 62 years of age
6 years or up to 65 years of age

questions.explanation: CEC and ECs: 6 years or up to age 65 whichever earlier. Removal of CEC: same procedure as a Supreme Court judge (by Parliament, requires special majority). Other ECs can be removed on the recommendation of the CEC. whichever is earlier.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Constitutional bodies (CAG, UPSC, EC) — mixed tiers

_fixes.was: 6 years or up to 65 years of age (whichever is earlier)
_fixes.now: 6 years or up to 65 years of age

questions.stem: Consider the following about the CAG. 1. CAG audits ALL receipts and expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India and of each State. 2. The CAG's salary is charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India. 3. After demitting office, the CAG is eligible for further office under the Union or any State government. 4. CAG is removed only through a process similar to that of a Supreme Court judge. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 3 is WRONG — after the CAG's term, he is NOT eligible for further office under the Union or any State (to preserve independence). 1, 2, 4 are correct — salary is charged (no parliamentary vote), removal procedure mirrors SC judge.
